title: The Data Patch
text:
Data modeling, planning, and structuring






NotePricing Example





Data Management Guidance Review  $175/hour x 2 hours = $350
Scenario: Your funding organization develops a 5-page data management guidance document for its grantees. Since it will be public and grantees will be expected to follow it, you want a second perspective on its validity and potential gaps. The Data Patch reviews the guidance and provides comprehensive feedback that goes beyond simple edits:

identifying strategic gaps
verifying and/or recommending discipline-appropriate repositories and metadata standards
suggesting resources to help grantees succeed

We help you transform general principles into actionable expectations with clear milestones, empowering your grantees to meet your standards with confidence.



Open your seed catalog, sharpen your tools and lay out your garden. Getting the structure right from the start saves enormous headaches later.
We help you design data that works: management plans that satisfy funders and set your future self up for success; well-documented models that reflect how your research actually operates and allow you to stand up a database; and collection templates aligned to standards so your data plays well with others.
What you get:

Data management plans that go beyond boilerplate
Data models tailored to your project’s needs
Collection templates aligned to community standards, making publishing, sharing, and reuse straightforward

Whether you’re starting a new project or organizing one that’s growing wild, we’ll help you build a foundation that lasts.

title: The Data Patch
text:
Data mobilization and publishing






NotePricing Example





Legacy Site Plant Inventory Mobilization and Publishing  $175/hour x 16 hours = $2,800
Scenario: Your land trust has five years of vegetation monitoring data (2018-2022) from multiple preserves stored in varied Excel formats with inconsistent species names and plot numbering. You want to publish this data to support regional conservation planning. The Data Patch handles the complete mobilization process:

cleaning and standardizing site codes, survey dates, and plot coordinates across all files
aligning plant names against taxonomic databases (e.g. COL)
transforming data into Darwin Core format with appropriate survey extensions
conducting quality validation and flagging any remaining data gaps
publishing to GBIF with full metadata documentation and DOI assignment

We help you rescue valuable monitoring data from scattered spreadsheets and transform it into a published, citable resource that demonstrates conservation impact and informs regional biodiversity initiatives.
Guided Mobilization Approach  $175/hour x 6 hours = $1,050
Alternative scenario: You have staff capacity to do the hands-on data work but need expert guidance to do it right. The Data Patch provides structured consultation across three sessions:

initial assessment of your data and recommended cleaning steps
guidance on taxonomic resolution tools and Darwin Core mapping strategies
review of your prepared dataset and support through the GBIF publishing process

This approach leverages your team’s time while ensuring you avoid common pitfalls, making it ideal when you have interested staff and want to build internal capacity.



The harvest is the most satisfying part of any growing season—gathering everything you’ve cultivated and putting it to use. We help you bring your data in from the field and share it with the world.
We handle the transformation, formatting, and publishing so your datasets become part of the broader scientific ecosystem—discoverable, citable, and ready to inform new research.
What you get:

Full dataset workup cleaning, validation, and quality checks
Persistent identifier assistance so your data stays findable
Taxon resolution to align species names with recognized authorities
Data transformation into standard formats (Darwin Core, ISO, and others)
Publishing to suitable repository like GBIF and/or OBIS, with DOI assignment
Legacy data mobilization older datasets deserve a place in the sun too

Every dataset represents real effort in the field and the lab. We help make sure that effort keeps bearing fruit.

title: The Data Patch
text:
Pricing
We’re upfront about pricing because we know good data management starts with realistic budgets. Whether you’re writing a grant or planning a project, having clear numbers leads to better outcomes for everyone.

Our base rate is $175/hour, but that’s just a starting point.

We price based on the work, the relationship, and the mission. Conservation research? Long-term partnership? Tight budget but important science? Let’s talk. We’d rather find a way to help than turn you away.
Think of our services as an à la carte menu. Each service comes in three sizes:

We advise — you do the work, we guide you
We collaborate — we work alongside you
We deliver — we handle it for you







A few things that help us lower our rate:

Bigger commitments: longer projects let us work more efficiently
Your involvement: if you’re doing the hands-on work and we’re advising, that’s less of our time
Work we believe in: we give deeper discounts to mission-driven projects




Scoping is always free. We’ll talk through what you need and give you an honest estimate before any clock starts.
Get in touch and we’ll figure out what works.

title: The Data Patch
text:
We believe data management makes the world a better place and every scientist should be empowered to shine at it.

Services to help you meet the requirements of modern science like the FAIR principles, CARE principles, and open science.

title: Who are we?
text:
The Data Patch is Abby Benson and Steve Formel. With a combined 25 years of data management experience, Abby and Steve have helped develop international and US national standards and practices for open data, implementing the FAIR principles, federal data management requirements, and cutting edge data types like eDNA, PAM, and telemetry.



Abby Benson 

Abby Benson started as an ecologist studying thirteen-lined ground squirrels on prairie dog colonies in Colorado before discovering her passion for data at USGS. A champion for making biodiversity data useful, her interest focuses on the drivers and effects of changing ecosystems on organisms at a national scale and the role management can play in mitigating harm.






Notelearn more…





Abby served as the node manager for OBIS-USA from 2018 - 2023 and the node manager for GBIF-US from 2019 - 2023. She has been heavily involved in data management communities like ESIP, TDWG, and the GBIF and OBIS communities. She has worked with the Marine Biodiversity Observation Network, Global Ocean Observing System, National Ecological Observatory Network, and many others to share their data to these global systems. She also launched the ESIP Biological Data Standards cluster in 2021 winning the ESIP Catalyst Award in 2022 and the Standardizing Marine Biological Data working group in 2019.







Steve Formel 

Steve Formel is a microbial ecologist by training, with past research focusing on the relationship between a salt marsh grass, its microbiome, and the Deepwater Horizon oil spill. In 2021 he turned his attention toward improving data management and standards implementation for large, complex data and projects.






Notelearn more…





Steve’s experience includes archiving data as a data officer for NOAA’s NCEI, developing and implementing data management solutions for large complex projects, like the Mesophotic and Deep Benthic Communities (MDBC) Restoration Portfolio and serving as the US node manager for OBIS and GBIF with the USGS. He currently serves as co-chair for the ESIP Biological Data Standards cluster and remains involved with TDWG and the Genomics Standards Consortium. He recently joined the OBIS Secretariat as a Data Officer, supporting the EU project, MARCO-BOLO.

title: The Data Patch
text:
We believe data management makes the world a better place and every scientist should be empowered to shine at it.

Most scientists don’t have a full-time data manager, but modern science expects you to manage data like you do. Whether you’re a do-it-yourselfer or looking to hand it all off to someone else, you need people who understand data ecosystems at different scales; and who can work quickly, within your budget.

We created The Data Patch as a place where you can pick your own solutions for the data management the world now expects. And if you’re not sure what that looks like, we’re happy to cultivate the whole thing for you: farm to table.


Read our Eos paper1 and watch our talk at the 2025 Living Data Conference2.

title: The Data Patch
text:
End-to-end support: planning, managing, publishing, and sharing






NotePricing Example





Multi-Year Monitoring Program: Design to Publication  $175/hour x 5 hours/week x 50 weeks = 250 hours = $43,750
Scenario: Your conservation organization is launching a new multi-site biodiversity monitoring program and needs comprehensive support from planning through first data publication. The Data Patch provides end-to-end partnership across the project lifecycle:

designing data collection templates aligned with Darwin Core and your specific monitoring protocols
developing a data management plan that satisfies funder requirements and sets up sustainable workflows
training field staff on data collection standards and quality control in a custom workshop
cleaning and mobilizing the first year’s monitoring data from all sites
publishing the inaugural dataset to GBIF with complete metadata and DOI
documenting reusable workflows and scripts for subsequent years

This comprehensive approach ensures your monitoring program is built on a solid foundation from day one, with your first dataset published and your team equipped to maintain data quality for years to come. The timeline estimate reflects the iterative nature of collaborative work: fewer hours if decisions move quickly, more if the program design requires extensive stakeholder input.



Farm to Table is our full-service offering: we handle everything from the first sketch of a data model to the moment your dataset is published and citable. But it’s not all or nothing. Think of our other services: Building Raised Beds, The Harvest, Pollinating, as options at a farmstand. Pick what you need, leave what you don’t, or let us put together the whole spread.
What you get:

Everything from our other services, combined to fit your project

Data modeling, templates, and management plans
Data cleaning, transformation, and publishing
Collaboration, training, and community engagement
Reusable scripts and documentation

A flexible approach—full service, à la carte, or anywhere in between

Some folks love getting their hands in the soil. Others would rather show up when dinner’s ready. However you like to work, we’ll meet you there. You set the table; we’ll help you fill it.

title: The Data Patch
text:
Education, engagement, and connection






NotePricing Example





Custom Workshop on Publishing eDNA Data  $175/hour x 12 hours = $2,100
Scenario: Your research lab has completed several eDNA sampling projects and wants to publish the data to GBIF and other biodiversity repositories. The Data Patch designs and delivers a half-day workshop tailored to your team’s workflow and data types:

reviewing relevant standards (Darwin Core, MIxS, GGBN extensions) for eDNA observations
walking through real examples from your projects to demonstrate data structuring and mapping
addressing lab-specific questions about metadata requirements and quality control
providing follow-up resources and publishing checklists

We help your team move from sequences and observations to shareable, citable datasets that contribute to global biodiversity monitoring and research.



In any garden, pollinators help everything grow stronger through connection. We can play a similar role in your data ecosystem, helping communities learn from each other and cultivate shared practices.
Whether you’re looking to train your team, bring together a working group, or strengthen ties across organizations, we help create the conditions for collaboration to flourish.
What you get:

Custom workshops on biological data standardization, designed for your community’s specific needs
Working group facilitation to keep collaborative efforts on track
Data development discussions for small teams navigating standards and workflows
Stakeholder engagement that brings the right voices to the table

Healthy ecosystems depend on connection. We help communities cross-pollinate ideas, standards, and expertise so everyone’s work can thrive.
